$comment: Hand-written half of the licence list. The npm half is generated by scripts/gen-licenses.mjs from node_modules. Every licence below was read from the named primary source; where a licence could not be verified the entry says so and points at the upstream project instead of asserting one. `npm run check:licenses` fails if a direct npm dependency has no `npm` entry or a direct Rust crate in src-tauri/Cargo.toml has no `crate` entry.

entries.name: Tauri
entries.usedFor: The desktop shell: the window, the command bridge between the interface and Rust, and packaging. The OS supplies the web view; Tauri's windowing crate (tao) is Apache-2.0 and its web-view crate (wry) is Apache-2.0 OR MIT.
copyright: Copyright (c) 2020-2023 Ngo Iok Ui & Tauri Programme within The Commons Conservancy (wry)
entries.holder: Tauri Apps Contributors; Tauri Programme within The Commons Conservancy
entries.basis: license field and LICENSE files of the tauri, tao, and wry crates as locked in src-tauri/Cargo.lock

entries.name: SQLite
entries.usedFor: Stores settings, progress, snapshots, and chat history on this device, and powers the packaged lesson search. Compiled into the app by rusqlite's bundled feature.
entries.holder: The SQLite authors, who dedicated the code to the public domain
entries.basis: sqlite.org/copyright.html

entries.name: llama.cpp
entries.usedFor: Runs the optional private local topic chat. Setup downloads this exact release for your operating system, checks its SHA-256, and starts it on a loopback port. It is not part of the installer.
entries.note: The release archives also contain third-party code under its own licences (the repository keeps one in licenses/LICENSE-jsonhpp for nlohmann/json). Check the upstream project for the full list.
entries.basis: LICENSE at release tag b10991 of ggml-org/llama.cpp; release and archive names from src-tauri/src/local_ai.rs

entries.name: Qwen3.5 2B (Q4_K_M, GGUF)
entries.usedFor: The language model behind the optional local topic chat. Setup downloads this immutable revision (about 1.3 GB), checks its SHA-256, and keeps it in the app's data folder. It is not part of the installer.
entries.holder: The Qwen team (Alibaba) for the model; Unsloth AI for the GGUF quantisation
entries.note: The file comes from huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.5-2B-GGUF, a quantisation of Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B. Both model cards declare Apache-2.0.
entries.basis: License field in the model card front matter of unsloth/Qwen3.5-2B-GGUF at the pinned revision, and the Apache-2.0 LICENSE file in Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B; model and revision from src-tauri/src/local_ai.rs

entries.name: Teaching models trained for this app
entries.usedFor: The small models that run inside the labs: a 1.37M-parameter two-layer character transformer, a character RNN, a bigram table, a sparse autoencoder, an MNIST VAE and a diffusion denoiser, with the interpretability caches, embedding projections, and tokenizer built alongside them. They exist to show mechanisms, not to be useful models.
entries.note: Trained by this project from the data listed under Data, so their status follows that data; see the MNIST entry, whose open question carries over to the two models trained on it. Training details are in models/MODEL_CARD.md in the project source.
entries.basis: models/MODEL_CARD.md and the training scripts under models/; the repository declares no licence for the app or these models

entries.name: Tiny Shakespeare
entries.usedFor: The shared character corpus the bigram table, RNN, transformer, sparse autoencoder, and tokenizer were trained on. The corpus file itself is not shipped; short excerpts appear in the sparse-autoencoder example cache.
entries.licence: Public domain (the works of William Shakespeare)
entries.holder: William Shakespeare (d. 1616); this copy is a transcription by others
entries.note: Pinned to commit 6f9487a of karpathy/char-rnn (SHA-256 86c4e6aa...). The repository's README says MIT for its code; at that commit it has no licence file and no provenance note for the text file, so the edition behind this transcription is not stated. Check the upstream project.
entries.basis: models/data/tiny-shakespeare.provenance.json, models/download_corpus.py, and the repository README and file listing at the pinned commit

entries.name: GloVe word vectors, 50 dimensions
entries.usedFor: The Tokens & embeddings lab ships the first 10,000 ASCII words from this set as vectors and two-dimensional projections. The copy was taken from the RaRe-Technologies/gensim-data release.
entries.holder: Jeffrey Pennington, Richard Socher, and Christopher D. Manning (Stanford NLP Group)
entries.note: Stanford publishes these vectors under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License v1.0 (opendatacommons.org/licenses/pddl/1.0/). They were trained on Wikipedia 2014 and Gigaword 5; the terms of those source corpora are not covered by that statement. Check the upstream project.
entries.basis: License statement on nlp.stanford.edu/projects/glove/, the same licence in the gensim-data dataset list, and models/prepare_language_assets.py

entries.name: MNIST handwritten digits
entries.usedFor: The VAE and the diffusion denoiser in the Diffusion & VAEs lab were trained on 20,000 digits from the MNIST training split. The app ships no MNIST images, only the trained models.
entries.holder: Yann LeCun, Corinna Cortes, and Christopher J.C. Burges; derived from NIST Special Databases 1 and 3
entries.note: We could not verify a licence from a primary source. The authors' page states only that the database was derived from the original NIST databases, and the dataset directory on that server was empty when checked. Secondary sources disagree (the Hugging Face mirror card says MIT, while this project's own training metadata recorded Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0 without a primary source), so none is asserted here.
entries.basis: yann.lecun.com home page and /exdb/mnist/ as served when this list was written, compared with the Hugging Face ylecun/mnist card and models/train_mnist_models.py
